Create the documented responsive component with semantic HTML.

introduction: Practice mobile-first; Bootstrap vs custom CSS; CDN/manual setup; local assets; CSS; JavaScript bundle using fictional school/student content.
explanation:
Bootstrap is a responsive front-end toolkit with a mobile-first grid, utilities and components. It accelerates consistent interfaces but does not supply a secure backend or replace HTML/CSS understanding. The viewport meta tag enables CSS viewport behavior on phones. Outside CodeLab, include one pinned Bootstrap CSS link and one bundle when needed; the bundle includes Popper for positioned plugins. Inside CodeLab local assets are preloaded and student CDN links/scripts are removed, so the manual setup example teaches external page installation without opening preview network access.

title: Containers, Grid, and Responsive Layout
objectives: Explain container/container-fluid/responsive containers using Bootstrap 5 conventions.
Create the documented responsive component with semantic HTML.
Test responsive behavior, keyboard access and the relevant interaction.
introduction: Practice container/container-fluid/responsive containers; row/col; 12-column grid; xs/sm/md/lg/xl/xxl; g/gx/gy gutters using fictional school/student content.
explanation:
Use a container around rows and columns inside each row. .container has responsive maximum widths; .container-fluid spans available width. Bootstrap 5 has six tiers: xs below 576 (no infix), sm ≥576, md ≥768, lg ≥992, xl ≥1200 and xxl ≥1400 pixels. .col-12 .col-md-6 .col-lg-4 gives one column on phones, two at md and three at lg. The 12-column system describes proportional widths, not 12 mandatory elements. Gutters set horizontal/vertical spacing with g-*, gx-* and gy-*; responsive variants can change them.

title: Typography, Colors, and Spacing
objectives: Explain headings/display/lead using Bootstrap 5 conventions.
Create the documented responsive component with semantic HTML.
Test responsive behavior, keyboard access and the relevant interaction.
introduction: Practice headings/display/lead; text alignment; fw/fst; contextual text/background; m/mt/mb/ms/me/mx/my/p/px/py; borders/rounded/shadows/width/visibility using fictional school/student content.
explanation:
Semantic heading tags describe hierarchy; .h1 or .display-* changes appearance without assigning semantic meaning. .lead introduces content; fw-* and fst-* adjust weight/style. Contextual colors need contrast checks, and status also needs text. Bootstrap 5 uses logical ms/me for margin start/end. Spacing utilities use a consistent scale, not arbitrary pixel numbers; responsive spacing variants start at their breakpoint. Borders, rounded corners and shadows support grouping. Width utilities and visibility must not hide essential information from keyboard or screen-reader users.
